program: University of Rome Tor Vergata — Integrated Building Design
description: Architectural and structural design of a two-level university library in reinforced concrete, formed by two overlapping rotated rectangular blocks.
body: An integrated architectural and structural design for a new university library with two levels and a basement garage, formed by two overlapping, rotated rectangular blocks in reinforced concrete with circular pillars and bidirectional slabs.

A steel structure supports the central staircase while a system of glulam beams carries the skylight; the terrace features a green roof, the envelope uses a ventilated façade, and the main entrance opens behind a glass façade. The project was developed in AutoCAD 2D, Revit and Enscape.

sections.title: Plans
body: Two levels over a basement garage, set out as two overlapping rotated rectangular blocks. Circular pillars and bidirectional slabs carry the floors; a steel structure holds the central staircase.

sections.title: Construction Details
body: The envelope resolved at 1:10 and 1:20: a green roof over the terrace, a ventilated façade around the blocks, and a glass façade at the main entrance. Each detail is keyed back to the section it is cut from.
